query: arxiv automated readability grade level control text generation education evaluation
note: On target. Candidates: 2407.01384 readability level control; 2309.05454 Flesch or Fumble; 2501.09158 GenAI text simplification for education.

claim: LLM judges exhibit self-preference bias, so a pipeline whose only subjective gate is the authoring model itself is not a review
result: CORRECTED - abstract retrieved (Wataoka, Takahashi, Ri, 'Self-Preference Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge'). The search snippet implied this paper recommends cross-family judging as the mitigation. It does NOT. It introduces a metric for the bias and attributes it to perplexity/familiarity: 'LLMs assign significantly higher evaluations to outputs with lower perplexity than human evaluators' and 'the self-preference bias exists because LLMs prefer texts more familiar to them.' No mitigation strategy is proposed in the abstract.
decision: keep, cite accurately (cite for the existence and perplexity-familiarity mechanism of self-preference bias; do NOT claim it endorses cross-family judges)

claim: instruction-tuned LLMs cannot reliably hit a specified readability band, so grade level must be measured independently rather than trusted
result: VERIFIED - abstract retrieved, 'Flesch or Fumble? Evaluating Readability Standard Alignment of Instruction-Tuned Language Models'. Evaluates models on story completion and narrative simplification 'using standard-guided prompts controlling text readability' against FKGL and CEFR, and finds 'globally recognized models like ChatGPT may be considered less effective and may require more refined prompts for these generative tasks compared to other open-sourced models such as BLOOMZ and FlanT5'.
decision: keep, cite in readability_and_vocabulary_control thread

claim: LLM judges favour both their own outputs and outputs from their own model family, which is the empirical basis for requiring a judge from outside the authoring family
result: VERIFIED - abstract retrieved, 'Play Favorites: A Statistical Method to Measure Self-Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge'. Proposes a framework that 'explicitly formalizes assumptions under which self-bias can be identified and estimated', controlling for true quality via independent human evaluation. Finds 'GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet, systematically assign higher scores to their own outputs' and that they 'display family-bias; systematically assigning higher ratings to outputs produced by other models of the same family.'
decision: keep, cite in multi_agent_llm_judge_review thread - this is the source that actually carries the family-bias claim, not 2410.21819

claim: LLM text levelling degrades at the lowest grade bands, which is the band this curriculum targets
result: VERIFIED - abstract retrieved, 'Evaluating GenAI for Simplifying Texts for Education: Improving Accuracy and Consistency for Enhanced Readability'. Simplifies from twelfth grade down to eighth, sixth and fourth. Quote: 'Both LLMs and prompting techniques demonstrated variable utility in grade level accuracy and consistency of keywords and key phrases when attempting to level content down to the fourth grade reading level.'
decision: keep, cite in readability_and_vocabulary_control thread - directly relevant because this run targets FK grade 2-6
